claims.text: Adding modest amounts of lightweight oxide-forming elements such as Al or Ti can produce a nanoscale microstructure in a lightweight high-entropy alloy.
The modified alloy will exhibit significant lattice distortion.
The oxide-forming additions will produce a coherent, protective surface oxide.
Lattice distortion hinders dislocation motion and thereby strengthens the alloy.
A stable, adherent surface oxide improves high-temperature oxidation and corrosion resistance.
The strengthening and protective-oxide benefits can be obtained while maintaining low density.
The baseline alloy produced by arc melting and homogenization forms a single-phase, for example FCC, solid solution with a uniform microstructure.
Combining increased Al or Ti content with tailored annealing will promote a fine-grained microstructure containing uniformly distributed nanoprecipitates.
The proposed intervention will promote a thin, coherent, surface-enriched oxide film.
The surface oxide is likely to be alumina or a complex oxide containing the lightweight element.
Lightweight oxide-forming additions increase the alloy's mixing entropy.
The added elements diffuse to the surface and form a fine protective oxide.
The protective oxide limits oxygen ingress and corrosion.
Relative to the baseline, the modified alloy will have higher tensile strength because of lattice distortion and grain refinement.
Relative to the baseline, the modified alloy will exhibit less oxidation weight gain at high temperature.
Relative to the baseline, the modified alloy will exhibit a lower corrosion rate in saline solution.
The modified alloy will retain a similarly low density or undergo only a modest density increase relative to the baseline.
The property benefits depend on maintaining the nanoprecipitate structure and oxide coherence.
At temperatures significantly above the oxide's stability range, exemplified as above 1000 °C, the proposed benefits will diminish.
In sufficiently corrosive environments that degrade the oxide film, the proposed benefits will diminish.
